subject.title: Crons ejecutaron mensajes de WhatsApp a la 1 AM fuera de horario y no se podían detener

question: Should this issue be resolved by splitting the schedule-activation replay fix from a separate emergency stop/delete design, or should one combined change define cron remove and gateway stop as an emergency outbound-delivery halt?
rationale: The replay bug has a concrete candidate PR, but the stop/delete expectation changes operator semantics across cron, gateway lifecycle, task cancellation, and channel delivery.

options.title: Land Replay Fix, Split Emergency Stop
options.body: Accept the schedule-activation boundary through the existing PR or an equivalent replacement, then sponsor a separate product-scoped emergency stop design.

options.title: Require One Combined Fix
options.body: Keep the issue open until one implementation covers restart replay, cron remove cancellation, and a gateway-level outbound halt.

options.title: Narrow To Replay Only
options.body: Treat stop/delete and emergency halt behavior as out of scope here and close only after the replay fix lands.

recommendation.title: Land Replay Fix, Split Emergency Stop
recommendation.body: Accept the schedule-activation boundary through the existing PR or an equivalent replacement, then sponsor a separate product-scoped emergency stop design.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has recent direct history on the candidate schedule-activation migration and already reviewed land-ready proof for the active PR.
